status: Fixed before full execution of this follow-up; prior native outcomes already known
question: Under declared field-access capabilities, can actual value-dependent recovery issue a checked replacement when access to an entire robust set is unavailable, while retaining failure and snapshot boundaries?
novelty_boundary: Existing work already executes logical recovery and SQLite replacement. This follow-up tests explicit capabilities, failure envelopes and adaptive completion under constrained access; not a new sufficient-reason principle or discovery of 29/85 native counts.

primary.population: Exactly the existing114 native heldout receipts across four previously selected weakening targets; all initially old-valid and robust additional set {profile,first_times}. Not new cases or holdout.
primary.selection: Match the preserved two-block class queries to all50931 original receipts. Independently rederive source/catalog selection and compare exact target-ID hashes.
primary.adaptive_policy: In the fixed P-before-T order, acquire a block only while the target verdict is ambiguous. Check declared capability before calling read. After each accepted complete response, re-evaluate target sufficiency. Stop as soon as determined. This is a specified policy, not globally optimal adaptive planning.
primary.robust_policy: Check availability/permission for the complete robust set before reads, then acquire that fixed set and check sufficiency. A deliberately conservative guarantee-first execution policy, not a strongest competitor or native OPA limitation.
primary.denominators: Two scenarios × two policies ×114 fixed case/target pairs =456 replay episodes, not456 independent source cases. No prevalence or latency estimate.

secondary.strict_full_cohort: All50931 old receipts; initial17442safe/33489insufficient; actual same-snapshot P recovery, target-bound replacement and independent raw label/sufficiency checks. Regression, not novel effectiveness evidence.
secondary.native_opa_controls: Three previously generated local OPA logs, separate from primary114 and heldout cohort; import then execute resulting receipt. Distinguish replacement after recovery, no-read replacement, and invalid old evidence refusal.

contract.source: Complete public derivative indexed after exact file checksum verification; actual block accessor returns a copied block and explicit binding envelope. No hidden full source is passed to the controller.
contract.trust: Declared local access capabilities and truthful complete source responses are assumptions. Digest equality is not authentication and this is not a production authorization service.
contract.success: A target-catalog-bound receipt is emitted only after the observed new fiber is nonempty and singleton; retained literals and exact base persist.
contract.failures: Denied or unknown access, unavailable source, callback exception, wrong case/snapshot/base/request binding, incomplete or unsupported block, retained-value conflict, invalid old evidence must not produce a claimed successful replacement.
contract.partial_work: Record permitted successful reads before a later failure; absence of a replacement does not refund them. Capability checks, callback attempts, accepted blocks, and zero-read replacements remain separate.
contract.storage: Serialized result ledgers for the experiment. No atomic/durable database transaction or real network source is claimed.

report: replacement sufficiency and raw label checks
measurement.excluded: No new performance benchmark. Full source hashing/indexing scans existing complete derivative in setup. Logical accessor counts are not total acquisition, network requests, physical I/O, or privacy savings.

independence: Independent checker uses separately expressed raw rule evaluation and finite completion enumeration; shares supported domain and public inputs. Adversarial capability/envelope scenarios are authored controls, not observed operational failure rates.
execution_freeze: Runner records this protocol and current source/test/checker hashes before batch execution. All outputs use new directories; retain failures without overwriting earlier evidence.
